rules.title: Service Boundaries Must Be Respected
rules.summary: Code should stay within the declared service or module boundary unless an explicit integration seam is defined and documented.
signals: direct imports across bounded service layers
hidden dependency on another service's private implementation
repo-local shortcuts that bypass documented integration contracts

rules.title: UI Layer Must Not Own Domain Orchestration
rules.summary: Presentation components should not become the place where multi-step business workflow, data branching, or orchestration logic accumulates.
signals: multiple API calls coordinated inside a page component
business branching embedded in rendering code
direct repository or database access from UI modules

rules.title: API Access Should Follow Approved Paths
rules.summary: Remote calls should use the agreed local abstraction for the target system rather than introducing bespoke access patterns in each feature area.
signals: repeated ad hoc HTTP client setup
duplicate auth or retry logic in feature code
multiple access shapes for the same upstream integration
exceptions: Client-wrapper modules (file stem ending _client/-client, e.g. product_core_client.py, ontology_context_client.py, api-client.ts) ARE the agreed local abstraction — remote-access markers inside them are not flagged. Naming-convention proxy, accepted for a medium/warn-tier heuristic; provenance mapp-pim PR #732 re-audit.

rules.title: Async and Eventing Patterns Must Be Consistent
rules.summary: Async workflows and event publication should follow the established pattern for the subsystem rather than mixing styles without explicit reason.
signals: event publication added without the expected wrapper or config seam
background tasks introduced in an inconsistent style
retries and failure handling differ across adjacent workflow code

rules.title: Estate Services Must Use the Canonical Event Stream
rules.summary: Services that publish or consume cross-app events must use the one canonical Kafka broker, canonical topic naming (mapp.{domain}.{entity}.{event_type}), the canonical CloudEvents-flavoured envelope from ct-events-schemas, and the canonical ct-events SDK. Bespoke brokers, topic names, envelopes, and Kafka clients are non-conformant.
signals: topic names not matching mapp.{domain}.{entity}.{event_type} (e.g. unprefixed product-event)
direct imports of bespoke Kafka clients (confluent-kafka, aiokafka, kafka-python, segmentio/kafka-go, kafkajs, node-rdkafka, rdkafka) instead of the ct-events SDK
per-service event envelope or schema definitions instead of consuming ct-events-schemas
a service producing or consuming cross-app events without an event_contract block in services.yml
canonical SDK pin missing or below the required minimum version

rules.title: Consumers Link to the Canonical Ontology, Never Embed a Divergent Copy
rules.summary: The estate has one canonical fashion ontology authority (fashion-ontology-service). Consumers declare an ontology_contract in services.yml linking to it (pinned canonical_version, non-local fallback) and must not embed a divergent ontology copy (ontology_complete.yaml / value_mappings.json) or re-implement a local Ontology/Canonicalizer. The authoring source (FLA) is exempt only via the SCP-owned allowlist, never by self-assertion. Enforced by SCP-R-013 (warn-baseline; DORMANT until the companion materialiser lands).
signals: an ontology consumer with no ontology_contract block in services.yml
ontology_contract.canonical_service is not fashion-ontology-service
an embedded canonical ontology file (ontology_complete.yaml / value_mappings.json) in a non-authoring repo
a local ontology re-implementation class (Ontology / OntologyLoader / Canonicalizer) in a non-authoring repo
ontology_contract.fallback resolving to a local ontology copy
exceptions: The authoring source is exempt from the embedded-copy / local-class signals, but ONLY via the SCP-owned ontology_authoring_allowlist (fashion-ontology-service, fashion-labelling-agent) injected by the materialiser — never via a self-asserted role field in the adopter's own services.yml.

patterns.title: Dashboard Pattern
patterns.summary: Use when a feature area needs a summary surface, scoped filters, explicit empty, loading, and error states, and a stable distinction between display logic and workflow logic.

patterns.title: Action Service Pattern
patterns.summary: Use when UI actions trigger meaningful business workflow so that orchestration, remote calls, and branching stay outside rendering code.
